lead.headline: Dolly Parton, country music's great ambassador, dies at 80
lead.dek: The singer, songwriter and philanthropist died in Nashville after a brief battle with cancer, her representatives said
body: Dolly Parton, whose seven-decade career carried her from a cabin in the East Tennessee hills to the head of an entertainment and philanthropic empire, died peacefully in Nashville on Tuesday at age 80. Her representatives said she had waged a brief battle with cancer, and her nephew confirmed the death.

Parton wrote her first No. 1 hit, "Joshua," in 1970 and topped the pop chart with the theme to "9 to 5," stacking up dozens of top-10 country records on the way to a 2022 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction. Her Dollywood theme park anchors the Smoky Mountains economy, and her Imagination Library mails a free book a month to children from birth to age 5.

Her philanthropy included a $1 million gift to Vanderbilt University Medical Center that helped fund Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine, and a Knoxville children's hospital was renamed in her honor. Her husband of nearly 60 years, Carl Dean, died in 2025. Tributes poured in Tuesday night from across music and public life.

briefs.headline: Graham wins South Carolina's GOP Senate runoff
briefs.summary: Appointed in July to her late brother Lindsey's seat, Sen. Darline Graham beat Rep. Ralph Norman with Trump's backing; pediatrician Annie Andrews awaits in November.

briefs.headline: Judge finds Postal Service violated mail-ballot order
briefs.summary: Indira Talwani said the administration 'cannot contend' it misread her injunction but let the rule publish Wednesday; USPS still cannot enforce it for November.

briefs.headline: Hawk Fire reaches 85% containment outside Reno
briefs.summary: The 15,067-acre fire has destroyed 47 homes and one business; about 5,000 people remain in evacuation zones, down from more than 90,000 at the weekend peak.

briefs.headline: Power shutoffs climb along with summer electric bills
briefs.summary: About 1 million U.S. households lost power over unpaid bills in August alone, NPR reports; Tulsa's utility disconnects at five times the national rate.

briefs.headline: Gang raid on Haitian hill town kills 47, dozens kidnapped
briefs.summary: More than 50 people were abducted Sunday from Kenscoff, above Port-au-Prince; 22 of the dead were executed in a church, and police opened a complicity inquiry.

briefs.headline: Nursery fire kills 14 newborns at Islamabad hospital
briefs.summary: An air-conditioner compressor exploded in the gynecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences early Wednesday; Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ordered a report within 24 hours.

briefs.headline: Injury count in French village tornado rises to 39
briefs.summary: About 300 homes in Pomas were damaged and its school partly destroyed; 20 people remain hospitalized and 1,400 Aude households were without power Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Iran and Oman agree on temporary Hormuz shipping lane
briefs.summary: The seven-mile corridor announced in Tehran runs partly through Iranian waters; Iran says the strait stays restricted until U.S. commitments under the June memorandum are met.

sections.label: West Virginia

briefs.headline: State mourns Parton, patron to 50,000 young readers
briefs.summary: Her Imagination Library mails free monthly books to about 50,000 West Virginia children; Gov. Patrick Morrisey called her 'a true American icon,' recalling her 2022 Clay Center visit.

briefs.headline: State cancels $63.5M DMV modernization contract
briefs.summary: Transportation Secretary Todd Rumbaugh pulled the AstreaX award as 'too costly' after lawmakers asked why a $30 million rival bid lost; a narrower rebid is planned.

briefs.headline: Hazelton workers cheer prisons deputy director's exit
briefs.summary: Josh Smith, the first senior Bureau of Prisons leader with a criminal record, resigned; the Hazelton union local cites 75% staffing and forced overtime.

briefs.headline: Kanawha paramedics log county's first field transfusion
briefs.summary: A county ambulance crew gave blood in the field five days after the program launched; its director says units can now intercept for neighboring counties.

regional.item: The fire marshal ordered six residences near Marshall vacated over structural and electrical hazards, and about 40 students moved to a downtown hotel.
Residents spoke three hours against Google's Buffalo data center, and commissioners said a state law leaves them no authority to stop it.
Parkersburg council voted down a widened $2,500-per-business grant program and advanced the water system expansion on second reading.

briefs.headline: Prince George-Valemount's Bird quits Conservative caucus
briefs.summary: Rosalyn Bird will sit as an independent, the third Conservative MLA to leave recently, saying parties should not overshadow the duty to constituents.

briefs.headline: Ottawa commits $38M to Nechako salmon hatchery
briefs.summary: The federal facility near the Fraser confluence, run with the Lheidli T'enneh First Nation, will raise 400,000 juvenile chinook a year; the final phase is due in spring 2028.

briefs.headline: Eby presses Ottawa for non-tariff measures against U.S.
briefs.summary: The premier asked British Columbians not to travel south and urged Canada to rethink a $12 billion fighter-jet buy and phase out U.S. thermal coal exports through Delta.

briefs.headline: Shingles vaccine tied to 24% lower dementia risk
briefs.summary: A Brown University study of 509,926 nursing-home residents found vaccinated adults diagnosed less often over four years; the authors caution causation is unproven.

briefs.headline: Manhattan-sized ice island breaks off Greenland glacier
briefs.summary: Sentinel-1 radar caught the 76-square-kilometer slab leaving Petermann Glacier on Aug. 4, its largest calving since 2012; two larger sections sit behind spreading rifts.

briefs.headline: Animal chromosomes evolve along one-way 'highways'
briefs.summary: A University of Vienna-led analysis of 5,800 genomes from 4,454 species finds chromosome fusions that mix genes cannot be undone, steering evolution along set paths.

briefs.headline: Gravity holds to Newton's law across galaxy clusters
briefs.summary: Researchers using the Atacama Cosmology Telescope found the inverse-square law holds across hundreds of millions of light-years, bolstering dark matter over modified gravity.

briefs.headline: Dutch lab lets riders adjust a robotaxi's driving in plain words
briefs.summary: TU Delft used GPT-4o-mini to tune a motion planner from passenger requests; it adjusted speed and comfort across eight prompts in simulation but offers no safety guarantees.

briefs.headline: Unclaimed 'Ox Alpha' model matches the industry's best
briefs.summary: The anonymous system appeared on OpenRouter Aug. 20 with a million-token context and coding scores near OpenAI's and Anthropic's top models; unconfirmed speculation points to China's Zhipu AI.
